author: Rob Loach
install_msg: Retro installed. Load it with `[p]load retro`, then attach a ROM to `[p]retro` and play. The emulator cores download themselves in the background and are detected automatically. Upgrading from a version before the cog class was renamed from RetroCog to Retro? Everything moves itself across on the first load; see the README.
name: Retro
short: Play retro console games in Discord
description: Play retro console games together in Discord. Start a game by name, URL, or an attached ROM or .zip (homebrew, or one you have the rights to) and control it with buttons under the screen. Eleven consoles are supported, from the Atari 2600 to the Super Nintendo, picked automatically from the file extension, each with its own controller layout. Every press posts an animated clip of the next few seconds, and Replay stitches the last fifteen seconds back into one. Games save automatically and pick up where they left off, even after the bot restarts and even after the channel has played something else: a save state restores the exact moment, the cartridge's own battery save is kept beside it so an in-game save survives an emulator core update, and a game a channel has moved on from keeps a Resume button. [p]retrosaves lists a channel's saved games, exports a battery save (or a save state) as a file to keep, imports one back after checking it against the real core, resets a game to its last in-game save, or wipes its progress entirely. Cores download themselves and are detected automatically, their own settings can be read and changed with [p]retroset coreoptions, and the bot owner can supply their own BIOS files (a whole zip of them at once) for cores that need one. Emulated through libretro.
end_user_data_statement: This cog stores the Discord channel and message ID of each game, the ID of the member who started it, the name of the game being played, and a copy of the ROM together with its emulator save state and the game's in-cartridge battery save, so a game can be resumed later. The same details are kept for the few most recent games a channel has moved on from, so their Resume buttons keep working. Recent gameplay clips are held in memory only, for the Replay button, and are lost when the bot restarts. Members with the Manage Messages permission, whoever started a game, and the bot owner can export a copy of a game's saves into the channel, replace them with an uploaded file, or delete them. Nothing is shared with anyone automatically. Cached ROMs, save states and battery saves are pruned automatically as a channel plays other games.
